result.summary: This PR fixes two out-of-bounds reads in the vendored UniValue JSON parser (src/univalue/lib/univalue_read.cpp): keyword matching via strncmp and a number-prefix check via firstDigit[1] could both read past the caller-supplied end pointer. It also updates the parse_univalue fuzz target and the UniValue unit tester to exercise bounded, non-null-terminated input so the fix is actually exercised. The change is small (34/-31 across 10 files) and closes tracked issue #28260.
result.problem: UniValue's getJsonToken function assumed the underlying buffer was null-terminated when matching keywords and validating number prefixes, so it could read past the end pointer supplied by the caller. This affects any consumer that parses untrusted or bounded (non-null-terminated) JSON buffers through UniValue, including RPC/HTTP request parsing.

open_concerns: maflcko has repeatedly pushed back on how the unit test buffers are constructed (avoiding hidden null terminators, avoiding trailing data from adjacent fixture strings), with the latest round of comments (2026-08-07) still unresolved after the most recent force-push.

sedited questioned whether most of the added unit tests are redundant given fixture files and the fuzz target already covering similar cases; this was partially addressed by removing the extra helper and squashing commits.
resolved_concerns: sedited's request to use std::string_view construction instead of pointer arithmetic was implemented by the author.
carloantinarella's request to squash commits was done by the author.
maflcko's earlier request to remove an unneeded ternary was fixed in a follow-up push.

categories.name: utils
categories.evidence: Directly modifies src/univalue/lib/univalue_read.cpp, a vendored subtree covered by this category, fixing a memory-safety bug in a primitive used across the codebase.
categories.rationale: Fixes a real out-of-bounds read against a caller-supplied end pointer in a widely used vendored JSON library, tracked as issue #28260 ('getJsonToken assumes underlying string is null-terminated but requires end pointer'). Category priority puts correctness and safety of primitives first, and this is exactly that kind of subtle, node-wide-reachable bug even though no crash or exploit has been demonstrated.

uncertainties: Whether the out-of-bounds read is practically exploitable (e.g. causes a crash or information leak) or is a benign over-read within allocated memory is not established in the discussion.

Whether the rpc category maintainers would actually consider this an rpc-area PR or purely a utils/subtree fix is unclear; the RPC/REST/ZMQ label is present but the change never touches RPC code directly.
The PR has had 7 force-pushes and ongoing test-construction disagreement; it's unclear how close it is to reviewer satisfaction on the test portion versus the core fix, which appears settled.
result.card: This PR fixes two out-of-bounds reads in the vendored UniValue JSON parser: keyword matching (strncmp) and number-prefix validation (firstDigit[1]) could both read past the caller-supplied end pointer, closing tracked issue #28260. It also reworks the parse_univalue fuzz target and UniValue unit tests to exercise bounded, non-null-terminated input so the fix is actually exercised. sedited gave a Concept ACK and carloantinarella a tested ACK on the core fix, with no objections to the change itself, but there is ongoing, still-unresolved disagreement with maflcko over how the unit test buffers should be constructed, most recently on 2026-08-07. The PR needs a rebase (mergeable_state dirty) and conflicts with an open PR (#36116). Given UniValue's role parsing RPC input, the bug is security-relevant but likely low severity in practice since RPC access requires authentication.
